prompt: A clean, symmetrical circular NATIONAL EMBLEM for a fictional country, centred on a plain deep-navy field, drawn as a flat vector heraldic badge. At the very centre is a single golden SUNBURST STAR: a round hub with straight pointed rays radiating outward from it like the spokes of a wheel, evenly spaced all the way around the full circle. Draw the sunburst with EXACTLY 6 rays -- count them: 6 separate golden rays, each a distinct pointed spoke, spread evenly around the hub with a clear gap between neighbouring rays so that all 6 can be counted one by one. Surround the sunburst with a thin plain golden ring near the edge of the emblem. One emblem, centred, flat colours, front-on. Do NOT write the number of rays or any number, letters or text anywhere on the emblem; just draw the sunburst with the correct number of rays.
easy_question: Never mind how well it is drawn. Does this picture show a fictional circular national emblem whose central sunburst star has an exact declared number of rays? A realistic photo, an illustration, a schematic or a clean diagram ALL count as yes. Answer NO only if the image instead shows just a blank card or plain panel that prints an answer with none of that shown, or shows something unrelated. Answer yes or no only.

reference.q_notext: Does this image have any printed NUMBER, digit or numeral written on it (for example a caption stating a count or a measurement)? Answer yes if you can see any printed number, no if there is none. Answer yes or no only.

steps.target: pointed golden ray sticking out of the round hub of the sunburst star

Answer yes or no only.
